title: FluencyCraft Advanced - Day 13
why_important: Handling crisis communications protects company reputation.

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): When talking about rescheduling a team sync (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My manager'?

options.a: Shift meeting 3 clock possible?
options.b: Shift meeting 3 clock possible? yesterday
options.c: I am rescheduling a team sync right now.
options.d: Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'order in'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: Request food delivered home.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'order in' means: request food delivered home. Example: "Let us order in dinner tonight."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'hedge against'?

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.c: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.c: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.
